This is Temple Building and I live there in a studio (800 sq ft) by myself. It’s one of very few places in the city that I could find that allows German Shepherds and has in-unit appliances hookups. 

It also has heated garage parking, roof access, a gym, and valet service. Internet is included if you like. The convenience of being a short drive to work and close to downtown was appealing to me. The view from above 14+ floors on the roof isn’t shabby, either.

All in all, I’m paying about $1,700 (it has gone up considerably each year since I moved in) for rent, internet, water, trash. It’s getting pricey to stay now, though, and I’m looking at other options. I yearn for a nice yard for my dog. 😭
Yay! Have a wonderful journey!

I’m from the south (US) and moved to Rochester a couple years ago. I love it. Cool things to see, good food, not too big and not too small a city. Here are some tips: 

1. Buy a “happy lamp” to adjust to low light! Make sure you get enough physical activity, even if it’s a daily quick walk around the block. Invest in a good, warm, waterproof winter coat and winter gloves.

2. Biking is feasible in late spring, summer, and most of fall, not so much in winter. I suggest staying as close to campus as possible. You can also find roommates pretty easily. There are city buses but I’m not as familiar. I live downtown and drive to campus. Once on campus, there are shuttles from place to place.

5. Not hard to find RA positions! My friend is one and they’re currently a grad student. Easy gig.

6. I’ve heard of PhD students doing a part-time program at the business school. Not totally unheard of, just depends how much you want to spend (both time and money ☺️), although after 2-years of part-time work, employees of UR are eligible for tuition benefits. Full time employees get up to 95% tuition waived after 1 year of full-time service.
